belief: Depression and anxiety are always caused by sin.
meta: A Christian look at the false belief that depression and anxiety are always caused by sin, with Scripture, questions, and homework for replacing it with the truth.
origins: Teaching that every emotional struggle comes from unconfessed sin or lack of faith. Well-meaning friends who asked, “What are you doing wrong?” when you were hurting. Not knowing that the body, the brain, life events, and loss all affect mood. Shame that made you hide your struggles. Times when a sin did make things worse, so you assumed it always must be the cause.
teaches: Sin can contribute to emotional pain, but Scripture does not teach that it is always the cause. When the disciples asked whose sin made a man blind, Jesus said neither. Elijah, a faithful prophet, became so exhausted and discouraged that he asked to die, and God responded with rest, food, and gentle care. Paul despaired even of life. Depression and anxiety can come from many sources: body, brain, loss, stress, trauma, thinking patterns, and spiritual struggles. God meets you in all of them.
self_statements: If I weren’t sinning, I wouldn’t be depressed.
My anxiety proves I don’t trust God.
I must have done something to deserve this.
God is punishing me with these feelings.
If I confess enough, this will go away.
Christians who are depressed aren’t right with God.
errors: Turning “sin can cause distress” into “all distress is caused by sin.”
Blaming yourself for something with many causes.
Deciding the cause without considering the body, stress, or loss.
Ignoring Bible heroes who struggled deeply without sinning as the cause.
Treating a painful condition as proof of moral failure.
questions: What did Jesus say when the disciples blamed sin for the man’s blindness?
Was Elijah’s despair caused by sin, or by exhaustion and fear?
Did God scold Elijah, or did He feed him and let him sleep?
What other causes could be affecting my mood: sleep, health, stress, loss?
Have I confessed and repented and still feel this way? What might that tell me?
Would I say this to a friend who was depressed?
Who first taught me that emotional pain always means sin?
truth: Depression and anxiety are not always caused by sin. They can come from my body, my brain, loss, stress, my thinking, or many other things. Faithful people in the Bible felt deep despair. God is near to the brokenhearted, and He meets me with care, not condemnation. I can seek His help and every good help He provides.
hw_questions: What did Jesus say about whose sin caused the blindness?
Was Elijah’s despair caused by sin or exhaustion?
What else could be affecting my mood?
Would I say this to a hurting friend?
hw_truths: Not all emotional pain is caused by sin.
God is near to the brokenhearted.
God meets me with care, not condemnation.
Faithful people in the Bible felt deep despair too.
I can look for every cause and every kind of help.
God heals the brokenhearted and binds up their wounds.
log: Each day, rate my mood from 0 to 10 and note sleep, food, stress, and activity. Look for patterns at the end of the week.
name_example: The LORD is near to Sarah when she is brokenhearted; He saves her when she is contrite in spirit.
actions: and list every way God cared for Elijah before He spoke to him about his mission.
Schedule a checkup with your doctor
and mention how your mood has been.
For three days, get regular sleep, meals, and a short walk,
Talk with a pastor or Christian counselor
prayer: Lord, thank You that You are near to the brokenhearted. Help me reject the lie that depression and anxiety are always caused by sin. Show me the true causes of my pain, lead me to the help I need, and let me feel Your care instead of condemnation. Heal my heart and bind up my wounds. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
